title: Introduce semantic-coverage gate and triggered patch-eval CI hook
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Add semantic coverage-based prompt-set gate to detect coverage regressions
Add CI hook to trigger targeted "patch-eval" when a gate fails
Expose per-cohort coverage metrics to the eval dashboard
description: Context: We observed subtle regressions where model outputs remained high-level correct but surface-level semantic coverage across prompt cohorts narrowed after model swaps/quantization changes. Existing numeric metrics and token-level deltas miss cases where the model no longer covers important semantic variants present in our prompt catalog. Motivation: Prevent silent degradation of prompt-set representativeness and provide an actionable CI path for fast, targeted investigation. This PR introduces a semantic-coverage gate and an associated triggered patch-eval CI hook. The gate computes an embedding-based coverage fingerprint per prompt cohort and compares the new model's semantic footprint to the baseline. If the coverage delta exceeds configured thresholds, the gate fails the CI run and automatically schedules a patch-eval that runs a focused battery of targeted tests (a subset of the full eval tuned to high-leverage prompts). What changed: - New gate: eval_harness/gates/semantic_coverage.py implements per-cohort coverage profiles, embedding fingerprint generation, and multiple comparison modes (jaccard-over-embeddings, centroid-distance, and top-k neighbor overlap). - CI hook: ci/hooks/triggered_patch_eval.py adds a lightweight runner that kicks off the patch-eval with deterministic sampling and collects aggregated reports. The hook supports backoff retries and a dry-run mode for manual investigations. - Dashboard integration: metrics/coverage_profiles/adapter.py and docs/ explain how coverage profiles surface in the eval dashboard and the thresholding configuration. - Tests: tests/test_semantic_coverage.py and a small end-to-end smoke test in ci/integration/smoke_semantic_coverage.yml. - Documentation: docs/eval_gates/semantic_coverage.md with rationale, recommended thresholds, and troubleshooting steps. Operational notes and rollout: - Default is OFF for main CI. The gate is enabled for the nightly-canary job and for release candidate pipelines. - Thresholds are conservative by default (0.15 centroid-distance / 20% top-k overlap), with a recommended calibration run per-model-family recorded in metrics/coverage_profiles/baseline_manifest.yml. - Patch-eval targets only changed cohorts and up to 200 associated prompts (configurable) to bound cost. Testing: - Unit tests cover embedding fingerprint correctness and comparison modes. - A simulated drift integration test verifies that the gate fails when we inject semantically distinct prompts. - CI: initial runs showed a flaky network call to the embedding service; added retry+timeout. Backwards compatibility: The gate is additive and non-breaking; enabling it requires toggling a pipeline flag. Implementation details and notes on design choices: - We cache cohort embeddings to S3-like object storage and use a TTL to balance freshness vs cost. - To reduce false positives from noisy embeddings, we aggregate across prompt paraphrases and use median-centroid comparisons rather than mean in the default mode. - The patch-eval runner is intentionally conservative: it runs with a time budget and returns partial results if budget exhausted, marking the gate with a ‘partial-run’ label for human follow-up. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with gate disabled by default. 2) Enable for nightly-canary for two weeks and collect baseline metrics. 3) Gradually enable on release candidate pipelines and tune thresholds. 4) After stable behavior for 30 days, enable for protected branch PRs. Links: Linear ENG-4782 (requirements); SUP-9123 (internal support ticket with regression traces).
